prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1027; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for side impact collision at intersection. Insured reports other vehicle entered intersection against signal and struck driver's side door. Police report requested. Claimant identified and listed as represented by counsel; all contact to be routed through attorney's office.

Entry 2: Received police report. Responding officer notes both parties gave conflicting accounts of signal phase. Independent witness statement obtained and indicates claimant vehicle had green light. Liability position under review, leaning toward other driver at fault pending photo evidence from scene.

Entry 3: Attorney's office sent notice of representation and letter of claimed injury. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash, with headaches and reduced range of motion. Medical records requested with signed authorization. Vehicle damage appraisal scheduled and rental coverage confirmed for claimant.

Entry 4: Medical records received from treating provider. Diagnosis documented as cervical strain with whiplash-type symptoms. Treatment plan includes physical therapy sessions and follow-up with orthopedic specialist. Records reviewed against prior history; no prior neck complaints noted in the file.

Entry 5: Attorney's office submitted demand package including itemized medical bills, wage loss documentation, and vehicle repair estimate. Demand exceeds current reserve and has been referred to supervisor for evaluation. Recommended next step is to request independent medical examination and schedule negotiation call with counsel.
